question.text: The Democratic Unionist Party has long been the majority party in Northern Ireland's parliament, which convenes at Stormont Castle in this capital city.
question.clue: In the 1970s, a terrorist group based on this city's Shankill Road slit the throats of numerous Catholic residents and their leader was later gunned down by the Provisional IRA.

swap.leadin: One of these structures in southern Ohio named for a serpent was once thought to be built by the Adena culture.
swap.text: Name these earthwork structures built by Native Americans. One of the best known of these structures was built by the Mississippian culture at Cahokia.
swap.clue: The largest "platform" example of these structures in North America is the "Monks" one in Illinois.

question.text: This organization tried to assassinate Thatcher by bombing the Brighton Hotel. This organization fought British and unionist forces during a period known as The Troubles.
question.clue: This group placed a bomb inside a fishing boat that killed the last Viceroy of India, Lord Mountbatten, and a member of this organization named Bobby Sands became a martyr after dying during a hunger strike.

swap.leadin: This nation held a referendum in May 2015 that approved same-sex marriage, the first nation to do so.
swap.text: Name this largely Catholic European country.
swap.clue: A civil war erupted in this country between pro and anti-treaty forces led by Michael Collins and Eamon de Valera, respectively.

question.text: The Irish Volunteers, led by Patrick Pearse, joined other rebel groups in this event. Roger Casement was charged with treason after this event.
question.answerHtml: Easter Rising [or Easter Rebellion or Éirí Amach na Cásca; prompt on the Rising or equivalents]
question.clue: James Connolly led the Citizen Army during this event, while the Volunteers were led by Patrick Pearse.

swap.text: The last portion of Gladstone's time as Prime Minister was dominated by granting this status to Ireland. This issue split the Liberal Party.
swap.clue: A policy known as "Killing With Kindness" was instituted by Arthur Balfour.

question.leadin: This movement provides its name to four bills, the third of which was passed in 1914 but never implemented due to World War I.
question.text: Name this movement calling for the self-governance of a former country of the United Kingdom.
question.answerHtml: Irish Home Rule [prompt on just “Home Rule”; prompt on “Irish Independence,” “Irish autonomy,” or other similar answers]
question.clue: Edward Carson and James Craig, leaders of the Unionists, campaigned against a 1914 bill aiming to bring about this outcome.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about Irish Home Rule.
swap.text: The Irish Parliamentary Party advocating Home Rule was founded by this member of Parliament whose career saw a scandal following his affair with Kitty O'Shea.
swap.clue: The reputation of this man was tarnished by a letter forged by Richard Pigott, which appeared to condone the murders of Thomas Burke and Lord Cavendish in Phoenix Park.

question.text: Followed shortly by an engagement at Beachy Head, it saw the Earl of Tyrconnell and Duke Lauzun retreat across the River Nanny at Duleek after taking heavy losses. Fought near Drogheda, for 15 points, name this 1690 battle in Ireland resulting from the Glorious Revolution, a victory for William III over James II on a namesake river.
question.clue: The outcome of this battle secured the work of the "Immortal Seven" and is celebrated during the "Glorious Twelfth."

swap.text: Forgeries falsely implicated this Irish Nationalist politician in the murders, leading to the downfall of his coalition with the Liberal party. His political career was ultimately undone by his affair with Kitty O'Shea.
swap.clue: The supposed Popish Plot would have targeted a king with this regnal name.

question.leadin: One king of this city, Sigtrygg Silkbeard, was reportedly followed by valkyries into the Battle of Clontarf, which took place outside this city.
question.text: Name this city, which was the centre of an area known as the Pale after the Norman invasion of this city's country.
question.clue: This city is named for a black tidal pool where the River Poddle meets the River Liffey.

swap.text: The sister of this Irish nationalist leader drowned in 1911. He was a leader of the Irish Parliamentary Party and an advocate for Home Rule. His reputation suffered when he was accused of having a role in the Phoenix Park murders.
swap.clue: From jail, this man negotiated an agreement with William Gladstone that included concessions for land tenants called the Kilmainham Treaty.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a common act of protest against Britain.
question.text: This man died while leading a ring of Irish republicans on a hunger strike at Maze Prison. His actions were prompted by Britain's decision to revoke the Irish prisoners' Special Category Status.
question.clue: Winston Churchill Boulevard in Tehran was renamed for this man, prompting the British Embassy to move their main address onto a side street.

swap.leadin: About ninety followers of Hugh O'Neill and Rory O'Donnell fled this region for Spain in what was called the "Flight of the Earls."
swap.text: Name this northeastern region of Ireland, which was later heavily settled by Protestant Scots. Its traditional flag features a red hand.
swap.clue: This province was the site of an early 17th century "plantation," in which James I settled thousands of Scots here.

question.leadin: A song called about this event is called "The Fields of Athenry."
question.text: Name this 1840s, event which saw a particular island's population drop by almost twenty-five percent due to death and immigration, all due to the failure of a crucial crop.
question.answerHtml: Irish Potato Famine [accept equivalents if they have Ireland and Potato; prompt on partial answers; accept Gorta Mor]
question.clue: The Baring Brothers and Company ordered shipments of corn in response to this event, but other relief efforts were stopped by Charles Trevelyan, who attributed this event to divine judgment.

swap.leadin: "'God save Ireland!' said the heroes / 'God save Ireland' said they all." Answer the following about Irish rebel music.
swap.text: Dominic Behan's song "Come Out Ye [these people]" asks them to tell their wives "...how the IRA made you run like hell away / from the green and lovely lanes of Killeshandra." This notoriously brutal auxiliary force opened fire at a Gaelic football match at Croke Park.
swap.clue: Lyrics by Dominic Behan invite these people to "show your wives how you won medals down in Flanders."

question.text: A small French army led by Jean Humbert proclaimed the Republic of Connacht after winning the Battle of Castlebar during this uprising, sometimes named for a secret society founded by Wolfe Tone.
question.answerHtml: Irish Rebellion of 1798 [or United Irishmen Rebellion; accept equivalents mentioning the year 1798; prompt on ‘98]
question.clue: The losing side of this conflict were defeated at the Battle of Vinegar (+) Hill, and France tacitly provided support for this revolt thanks to the efforts of Wolfe Tone, who died before his planned execution after this event.

swap.leadin: Because Francis Needham's reinforcements arrived too late to forestall the losing side's retreat, it wasn't a total defeat for the Wexford rebels.
swap.text: Name this camp which was attacked by Gerard Lake's army on June 21, 1798.

question.text: In 1889 Parnell was politically ruined when his affair with this longtime mistress was revealed. Her husband, an Irish MP, filed for divorce and named Parnell as corespondent.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Prime Minister H.H. Asquith.
swap.text: In this 1914 incident during Asquith's premiership, 61 officers in the British Army resigned over rumors that they might have to fight Ulster Unionists over the implementation of Irish Home Rule.
swap.clue: This 1914 event in which 57 officers of the British Forces in Ireland elected to give up their posts.
